scene_description: A small tiled bedroom with a foreground bed, white open shelving and a narrow cabinet along the back wall, two floor lamps, a doorway, and white furniture at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial image shows a dark, narrow doorway with only a slim pale strip at its right edge; the broad angled wooden door leaf visible in the reference is absent from view.
candidate_target_observations: The candidate introduces a pale paneled door leaf in the doorway. Its front-facing, nearly vertical rectangular silhouette is much narrower and less oblique than the reference's open leaf, which projects down and right into the room and overlaps the foreground area. The candidate leaf remains behind the bed in image space rather than producing the same prominent foreground occlusion.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The candidate's shelves, cabinet, lamps, bed and door read as distinct objects arranged in a room. The door appears upright, but its displayed angle and projected extent do not match the reference. RGB views alone do not establish hinge attachment, contact, or collision.
new_visible_defects: The added door appears almost flush and front-facing compared with the strongly angled reference door, leaving the reference's large diagonal foreground silhouette missing. No other clear new defect is established by these views.
other_changes: The candidate cabinet has transparent-looking upper panels, closer to the reference than the initial opaque upper doors. The candidate also has a warmer illuminated patch around the rear lamp. Both reconstructions retain a simplified flat gray floor, pale uniform furniture and a simplified bed, rather than the reference's mottled floor, wood grain and richer lighting. The candidate viewpoint is wider and more frontal, with the right white furniture substantially less foreground-dominant than in the reference.

evidence.description: Large angled wooden paneled door projects into the room and creates a prominent diagonal foreground silhouette.
Dark narrow doorway and slim pale edge, without a visible broad door leaf.
Pale paneled leaf is visible but appears narrow and nearly front-facing, without the reference's extended diagonal projection.
Open shelves, narrow glazed cabinet and two lamps form a similar back-wall grouping to the reference.
Foreground bed and large right-side white furniture occupy much of the view, with mottled floor visible near the door.
Bed and right-side furniture are rendered against a comparatively uniform gray floor; the right-side object occupies less foreground area.

uncertainty: The target is inferred from the visible bedroom door differences; no explicit target defect was supplied. Different viewpoints affect apparent door width, angle and overlap, so the remaining mismatch cannot by itself prove incorrect underlying geometry. Overall improvement reflects the visible door and cabinet changes, not a verified mesh or lighting comparison.
